title: Triveni Ghat Rishikesh - Ganga Aarti, Timings & Travel Guide
content:
Triveni Ghat - Rishikesh,

Triveni Ghat is the most famous and sacred bathing ghat in Rishikesh, Uttarakhand, situated on the banks of the holy Ganga River. The name Triveni signifies the confluence of three sacred rivers - Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati, making this place highly revered among Hindus.

Taking a holy dip at Triveni Ghat is believed to wash away sins and bring peace of mind. Each day, hundreds of pilgrims and travelers come here for rituals, prayers, and to soak in the divine atmosphere of Rishikesh.

The most enchanting experience is the Ganga Aarti held every evening. As priests chant Vedic hymns and wave oil lamps, devotees float diyas (earthen lamps) on the river. The glowing sight of the Ganga lit with thousands of lamps creates an unforgettable spiritual experience.

According to mythology, Lord Krishna visited this place after being struck by a hunter’s arrow. The ghat is also surrounded by ancient temples like Gita Mandir and Lakshminarayan Temple, adding to its religious importance.

For travelers, Triveni Ghat is not only a spiritual hub but also a place to witness Indian traditions, devotion, and the soul-stirring power of the Ganga.

Best Time to Visit Triveni Ghat Rishikesh:

  • Peak Season (October - March): Pleasant weather with average temperatures 10°C - 25°C. Best for sightseeing, attending Ganga Aarti, and temple visits.
  • Moderate Season (April - June): Warm and sunny, with temperatures 20°C - 35°C. Ideal for spiritual visits and shopping, but carry cotton clothes and water.
  • Low Season (July - September): Monsoon season with average temperatures 18°C - 30°C. River levels rise and currents are strong, but the lush greenery makes the area scenic and peaceful.

Things to Do at / Near Triveni Ghat:

  • Take a holy dip in the sacred Ganga.
  • Attend the mesmerizing evening Ganga Aarti.
  • Visit nearby temples like Gita Mandir and Lakshminarayan.
  • Explore local street food stalls near the ghat.
  • Shop for souvenirs and handicrafts in nearby bazaars.

How to Reach Triveni Ghat:

  • By Road: Just 1 km from Rishikesh bus stand; easily accessible by auto or taxi.
  • By Train: Rishikesh railway station is about 1.5 km away.
  • By Air: Jolly Grant Airport (Dehradun) is 20 km away.

Best Places to Visit Near Triveni Ghat (within 50 km):

1 Ram Jhula (2 km): Famous suspension bridge with ashrams and cafes.

2 Laxman Jhula (4 km): Another iconic hanging bridge surrounded by temples.

3 Parmarth Niketan Ashram (2.5 km): A global yoga and spiritual retreat.

4 Beatles Ashram (4 km): Known for murals, meditation, and The Beatles’ visit.

5 Neelkanth Mahadev Temple (32 km): A revered Shiva temple in the forest.

6 Rajaji National Park (17 km - Chilla Gate): Great for wildlife safaris.

7 Har Ki Pauri, Haridwar (25 km): Famous for Ganga Aarti and holy dips.

8 Daksha Mahadev Temple, Kankhal (28 km): Mythological temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.

9 Mansa Devi Temple, Haridwar (27 km): Hilltop temple with ropeway access.

10 Chandi Devi Temple, Haridwar (30 km): Another Shakti Peeth, ideal for pilgrims.
excerpt: The Triveni Ghat Rishikesh is a sacred confluence of Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati, famous for holy dips and the evening Ganga Aarti. With nearby attractions like Ram Jhula, Beatles Ashram, and Rajaji National Park, it is a must-visit for pilgrims, nature lovers, and spiritual seekers.
